docs.title: LLM evals that don't get in your way
docs.text:
OpenEval is a lightweight, code-first evaluation framework for LLM outputs. You bring a model callable and a dataset; OpenEval runs an eval loop and returns a typed summary.

from openeval import EvalCase, run
from openeval.scorers import exact_match

cases = [EvalCase(input="2+2", expected_output="4")]
summary = run(lambda _: "4", cases, {"exact": exact_match})
print(summary.pass_rate)  # 1.0

Quick install

pip install openeval

docs.title: Why OpenEval
docs.text:
• Scorers are plain Python functions (no YAML, no inheritance)
  • Model-agnostic: OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama, or your own callable
  • CI-first: pytest plugin + GitHub Action to run evals on every PR

Badges (wire these up when you publish):

  • PyPI version
  • Python versions
  • License
  • GitHub stars

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
• openeval.run(model_fn, dataset, scorers, pass_threshold=0.7) -> EvalSummary
  • openeval.arun(model_fn, dataset, scorers, pass_threshold=0.7, concurrency=10) -> EvalSummary

docs.title: Batch
docs.text:
• openeval.batch.batch_run(model_configs, dataset, scorers) -> dict[str, EvalSummary]
  • openeval.batch.compare(summaries) -> ComparisonTable

docs.title: Dataset loaders
docs.text:
• openeval.dataset.from_csv(path, input_col="input", output_col="expected_output") -> list[EvalCase]
  • openeval.dataset.from_jsonl(path) -> list[EvalCase]
  • openeval.dataset.from_list(data) -> list[EvalCase]

docs.title: Scorers
docs.text: • exact_match, contains, regex(...), semantic_sim, llm_judge(...)

docs.title: Adapters
docs.text:
• openai_adapter(...), anthropic_adapter(...), ollama_adapter(...), callable_adapter(...)
  • Async variants: openai_async_adapter(...), anthropic_async_adapter(...), ollama_async_adapter(...)

docs.title: Reporting
docs.text: • openeval.generate_report(summary, output_path, title="OpenEval Report")

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
All example scripts live in openeval/examples/.

  1. 01_basic_qa.py — basic Q&A eval (no API key needed)
  2. 02_openai_eval.py — OpenAI eval + HTML report (uses OPENAI_API_KEY if set)
  3. 03_compare_models.py — compare two models with batch_run + ComparisonTable
  4. 04_rag_eval.py — evaluate a RAG pipeline
  5. 05_chatbot_eval.py — evaluate multi-turn chatbot behavior
  6. 06_code_eval.py — evaluate code generation
  7. 07_custom_scorer.py — write custom scorers from scratch
  8. 08_cicd_integration.py — CI/CD integration (pytest plugin + GitHub Action)

docs.title: The mental model
docs.text:
• A model is a callable: prompt: str -> output: str
  • A scorer is a callable: (input, output, expected) -> float (0.0–1.0)
  • A dataset is a list of EvalCase

docs.title: What you get back
docs.text:
run() returns EvalSummary with per-case results, scores, and a pass rate.

from openeval import EvalCase, run
from openeval.scorers import contains

cases = [EvalCase(input="Say hello", expected_output="hello")]
summary = run(lambda _: "hello world", cases, {"contains": contains})
print(summary.results[0].scores)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install openeval

Optional extras:

  • Semantic similarity scorer: pip install "openeval[semantic]"
  • OpenAI adapter: pip install "openeval[openai]"
  • Anthropic adapter: pip install "openeval[anthropic]"

Docs dependencies:

pip install mkdocs-material "mkdocstrings[python]"

docs.title: Quick Start (5 minutes)
docs.text: This page gets you to your first eval with no API keys.

docs.title: 1) Install
docs.text: pip install openeval

docs.title: 2) Run a minimal eval
docs.text:
from openeval import EvalCase, run
from openeval.adapters import callable_adapter
from openeval.scorers import exact_match, contains

cases = [
    EvalCase(input="What is 2+2?", expected_output="4"),
    EvalCase(input="What is the capital of France?", expected_output="Paris"),
]

mock_model = callable_adapter(lambda p: "4" if "2+2" in p else "Paris")
summary = run(mock_model, cases, {"exact": exact_match, "contains": contains})

print(f"Pass rate: {summary.pass_rate:.0%}")

docs.title: Using Adapters
docs.text: Adapters turn a model API into a simple callable.

docs.title: OpenAI
docs.text:
from openeval.adapters import openai_adapter
model = openai_adapter(model="gpt-4o-mini")

docs.title: Anthropic
docs.text:
from openeval.adapters import anthropic_adapter
model = anthropic_adapter(model="claude-sonnet-4-20250514")

docs.title: Ollama
docs.text:
from openeval.adapters import ollama_adapter
model = ollama_adapter(model="llama3.2")

docs.title: Callable
docs.text:
from openeval.adapters import callable_adapter
model = callable_adapter(lambda prompt: "hello")

docs.title: Async adapters
docs.text: For parallel evaluation, use *_async_adapter(...) with arun().

docs.title: Async Evaluation
docs.text:
Use arun() to evaluate many cases in parallel.

import asyncio
from openeval import EvalCase, arun
from openeval.scorers import exact_match

cases = [EvalCase(input="2+2", expected_output="4")]

async def model(_prompt: str) -> str:
    return "4"

summary = asyncio.run(arun(model, cases, {"exact": exact_match}, concurrency=20))
print(summary.pass_rate)

Tip: set concurrency based on your provider rate limits.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
openeval run --suite factuality --model callable:my_models:model
openeval run -d examples/data/basic_qa.jsonl -m ollama:llama3.2

docs.title: Async mode
docs.text: openeval run -d data.jsonl -m openai:gpt-4o-mini --async --concurrency 20

docs.title: HTML report
docs.text: openeval run -d data.jsonl -m callable:my_models:model -o report.html

docs.title: Loading Datasets
docs.text:
OpenEval can load datasets from CSV and JSONL.

from openeval.dataset import from_csv, from_jsonl

cases = from_jsonl("data.jsonl")
cases = from_csv("data.csv", input_col="input", output_col="expected_output")

docs.title: JSONL format
docs.text: {"input": "What is 2+2?", "expected_output": "4"}

docs.title: GitHub Action
docs.text:
The official action lives in the openeval-action/ folder in this repo.

Minimal workflow:

name: LLM Eval
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  eval:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: your-username/openeval-action@v1
        with:
          suite: hallucination
          model: openai:gpt-4o-mini
          threshold: "0.8"
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

Notes:

  • Ollama requires a self-hosted runner.
  • The action writes an HTML report and posts a PR comment.

docs.title: Writing Scorers
docs.text:
Scorers are just Python callables:

def scorer(input: str, output: str, expected: str = "") -> float:
    ...

Guidelines:

  • Return a float in [0.0, 1.0]
  • Be deterministic (avoid randomness)
  • Keep it fast (you’ll run this N×cases×models)

docs.title: Example: length constraint
docs.text:
def max_len(limit: int):
    def s(_input: str, output: str, _expected: str = "") -> float:
        return 1.0 if len(output) <= limit else 0.0
    return s

docs.title: Eval Suites
docs.text:
Suites are prebuilt datasets + scorers you can run in one line.

from openeval.suites import factuality
summary = factuality.run(lambda _: "Paris")

Suites included:

  • hallucination
  • factuality
  • instruction_following
